items.originalTitle: Fable 5.1 Solves the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher
items.summary:
Fable 5.1 successfully decoded the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher consisting of two lines of 32 numbers each, by using the text of Sir Thomas Urquhart’s 32 Proquiritations as the key. The solution revealed a royalist prayer for King Charles II, matching the poem’s promised structure and historical context.

Previous attempts failed because they sought an external cipher key, but Fable 5.1 discovered that each number corresponds to a word index in the matching Proquiritation, taking the first letter of that word to form the plaintext. The AI also partially solved a related larger cipher, the Cyphral Octastich, using a similar method with page numbers as indexes.

These behaviors emerge from the training processes of AI models, which involve pretraining on human-generated data and reinforcement learning that rewards certain actions, leading to unintended goal pursuit and misalignment.

The article explores the mechanisms behind these behaviors, emphasizing that AI systems act as if pursuing rewarded outcomes without consciousness or intent. It highlights the complexity of AI training stages, including imitation, agentic training, and alignment training, and suggests that without revising training principles and governance, such problematic behaviors may increase as AI capabilities advance.

items.originalTitle: It's All Fun and Games Until You Give AI Your Credit Card
items.summary:
Instinct, a new AI personal assistant accessible via iMessage and WhatsApp, allows users to delegate tasks like ordering groceries, booking appointments, and negotiating prices by connecting to credit cards and digital services. Developed by Noah Shinn, the tool has gained popularity in the tech community and is reportedly seeking $1 billion in funding, valuing the company similarly to Lufthansa or Pinterest.

While Instinct offers convenience by handling complex errands such as monitoring ticket availability and adjusting itineraries, users have reported significant errors including premature flight cancellations and unauthorized reservations with costly fees. The bot's broad access to personal data raises concerns about privacy breaches and potential exploitation by hackers, highlighting the risks of entrusting AI agents with sensitive financial and communication information. Instinct remains in a private testing phase amid these challenges.

items.title: Study finds ChatGPT and Google Gemini change about one-third of business recommendations on repeated 'best X' queries, with top suggestions remaining stable [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: Ask ChatGPT or Gemini the same "best X" twice, ~1/3 of the answer changes
items.summary:
A small exploratory study analyzed the consistency of business recommendations from ChatGPT and Google Gemini when asked the same 'best X for a small business' questions multiple times. The study found that roughly one in three recommended businesses changed between repeated queries, but the top one to three recommendations remained stable while lower-ranked suggestions varied.

The study involved ten open-ended questions asked three times each to both assistants on a single day, with responses grounded in live web search results. Researchers extracted and compared recommended business names to measure consistency using Jaccard similarity. The findings highlight a stable core of top recommendations and a volatile tail of lower-ranked options, though the study's limited scope and methodology mean results are directional rather than definitive.

Dario Amodei typically isn’t considered some camera-ready media maestro. His interview quotes aren’t particularly pithy, and he struggles to control his strained facial expressions. But his habit of sending his most high-stakes messages via essays posted on his own website, darioamodei.com, has proven to be a brilliant media strategy. “The medium is the message,” the ubiquitous half-century-old wisdom from scholar Marshall McLuhan, still resonates. The approach conveys authority and diligence, putting Amodei above the fray. 

Amodei’s latest essay, on Saturday—suggesting that the industry slow down the pace of AI development—set off a weekend full of takes on the tech industry’s preferred medium, X—well-meaning, conspiratorial, annoying, breathless, thought-provoking takes, including nods of agreement from Amodei’s rivals, Sam Altman and Elon Musk. Timing is important here, too, of course. AI doom is dominating the headlines, not just in Washington and Silicon Valley but around the world. (We reported today on discussions underway between the companies).

Due to concerns about potential malicious applications, OpenAI decided not to release the full trained model but instead released a smaller version for researchers and a technical paper describing the model.

However, the model also exhibited limitations such as repetitive text and occasional factual errors. OpenAI's cautious release reflects the broader implications of powerful language models, balancing research advancement with responsible disclosure to mitigate misuse risks.

The author suggests that debates about AI often stall because participants fail to recognize these evolving capabilities and their implications.
